evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This page mockup shows the system state after viewing history, which may be relevant if postconditions include displaying historical data; however, it does not directly relate to the outcome of retracting a confirmed bid.

evidence_cards.content: If the Customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item will be returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

source_locations.location: Process section, bullet point starting 'If the customer does not respond...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a terminal system state (item returned to inventory) triggered by time-based non-response in an alternative flow, which serves as a postcondition for that variant path.

evidence_cards.content: Clicking on the 'No Thanks' button releases the item from a hold status back into auction available inventory.

source_locations.location: Section 3) Decline Option

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the immediate observable system state change (release from hold to available inventory) upon successful completion of the decline action.

evidence_cards.content: If a bid retraction is not possible because the auction has ended or the bid was already superseded by a higher bid, the system displays an error message to the Customer indicating that the bid cannot be retracted.

source_locations.location: Exception Flow section, bullet point 2

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the system state after a failed retraction attempt — which is NOT a successful postcondition. Since no evidence on this page describes what happens AFTER a SUCCESSFUL retraction (e.g., 'bid is removed from active bids', 'customer is no longer bound'), there is NO concrete evidence for the postconditions slot of a successful use case.

evidence_cards.content: The system prevents bid retraction if the user is currently the highest bidder on an item.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Again, this describes a failure condition and prevention mechanism — not a successful outcome. Therefore, no valid postcondition claim can be extracted for the successful path.

evidence_cards.content: If someone cancels a bid, which may be a winning bid, then the next person in line would - in theory - be the winner.

source_locations.location: Bid Retraction definition paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system state change regarding auction leadership after a successful retraction (postcondition: next bidder becomes theoretical winner).

evidence_cards.content: The system has no way of following up to notify or offer second-place finishers; and even if we did, THAT person may no longer be interested in the item.

source_locations.location: Bid Retraction definition paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the post-retraction limitation on system actions (no automatic notification or status update for the new leader), confirming that the only state change is the shift in theoretical winner without downstream automation.
